title: SEA-Guard: Culturally Grounded Multilingual Safeguard for Southeast Asia

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating safeguard models on culturally grounded datasets (such as SEA-SafeguardBench) to measure their ability to accurately identify sensitive or harmful content specific to Southeast Asian norms, traditions, and localities.

Comparing the safety classification performance (AUPRC) of safeguard models across 8 different Southeast Asian languages and English to evaluate cross-lingual consistency and detect disparities in under-resourced languages.

Generating red-teaming prompts specifically designed to test the models' handling of sensitive information and potential stereotypes related to religious practices and food prohibitions (e.g., Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism) within regional contexts.
